text:
jordan: Heads-up: I'm proposing a small-but-impactful change to analytics storage for console routing/quotas telemetry. Current shape mixes routing policy info into a freeform `route` JSON blob which makes joins and rollouts painful. Suggest we add explicit columns and a migration plan so dashboards + rollouts can query efficiently.

maya: can you sketch the new shape? curious what breaks in existing dashboards.

jordan: rough idea: add `routing_policy_id` (uuid), `fallback_policy` (text), and `quota_config_v2` (jsonb) to analytics.events. Keep `route` blob for compatibility but stop writing new routing details into it. That lets queries do `WHERE routing_policy_id = X` instead of expensive jsonb->> ops.

liam: sounds reasonable. main ops concerns: backfills, index bloat, and long-running migrations on the events table (we're at ~1.2B rows). Need a no-downtime plan.

jordan: yep. plan I sketched: 1) Add nullable columns + indexes concurrently. 2) Start shadow writes from service (both hosted and dedicated) so new rows are populated. 3) Rollout console/ingest clients to read new columns when available. 4) Backfill in batches into historical partitions (offline job that writes to partitions rather than a full table rewrite). 5) Deprecate writes to route blob after verification.

rebecca: How are we going to surface progress to product? They want to do a canary rollout of the new routing UI that depends on `routing_policy_id`. We need an ETA on when canaries can start querying the new columns.

jordan: with shadow writes we should be able to run canaries within ~2 weeks (code + infra + monitoring). Backfill will be separate; canaries don't need historical data for initial rollout.

liam: indexing: we'll want a partial index on recent partitions and a global index on `routing_policy_id`? Partial index helps queries that only look at last 90 days. Also we should consider a multi-column index `(routing_policy_id, created_at)` for dashboards that aggregate by day.

maya: dashboards: Product analytics uses `route->>'policy'` in a few core queries. We'll need to update Looker/Metabase dashboards to point at `routing_policy_id` and add join helpers. Might be a good time to add a derived table `analytics.route_index` as a single source of truth for joins.

jordan: Agree on derived table idea. It can be a small materialized view we maintain via streaming job that compacts route metadata for quick joins. That will also help dedicated deployments that want to keep payloads smaller.

rebecca: QA checklist suggestion: - Shadow write verification (sampler that asserts parity between route blob and new columns) - Dashboard smoke tests (top 10 queries compare results) - Canary UX check on dedicated tenant - Latency regression test for writes

liam: For the backfill approach: do NOT run an UPDATE over the whole table. Instead: create a backfill worker that reads from historical partitions, writes new rows into a shadow copy partitioned by date, then swap partitions. Or, simpler, write individual UPDATEs in small windows with `DELETE/INSERT` into a re-created partition if our DB supports it. Need to profile.

jordan: example DDL I'd run (concurrent ops):

```sql
-- add columns and indexes concurrently
ALTER TABLE analytics.events ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS routing_policy_id uuid;
ALTER TABLE analytics.events ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS fallback_policy text;
ALTER TABLE analytics.events ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS quota_config_v2 jsonb;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_routing_policy ON analytics.events (routing_policy_id, created_at DESC);
```

and a small parity check job: 
```js
// pseudo
const sample = db.query(`SELECT id, route, routing_policy_id FROM analytics.events WHERE created_at > now() - interval '7 days' LIMIT 1000`)
for row in sample: assert(extractPolicy(row.route) == row.routing_policy_id)
```

rebecca: Nice. Who owns the migration job? Need to assign on the RFC.

jordan: I can own the migration orchestration. Liam can own the DB-side tooling and profiling. Maya to coordinate dashboard changes and product QA. Rebecca to own canary plan with customers.

liam: One more internal API debate: should we store `quota_config_v2` as expanded columns (limit, window_seconds, tier_id) instead of jsonb? Pros: faster filtering and smaller indexes for quota evaluation. Cons: schema churn for future quota fields. I'm leaning toward explicit columns for the hot-path quota checks and keep jsonb for extended metadata.

maya: yeah, for console quota UI we need explicit fields anyway to show usage and thresholds. If we add `quota_limit` (int), `quota_window_s` (int), `quota_tier` (text) that's probably enough. Keep `quota_config_v2` as the raw blob for future features.

jordan: good call. Update DDL to include those natived fields.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline note: adding concurrent indexes will increase IO. Recommend running during low-traffic window and throttle background jobs.

liam: I'll run a small test on staging with a snapshot of the events table and simulate the concurrent index build to measure impact.

rebecca: timeline proposal: Week 1: add columns + concurrent indexes; Week 2: shadow writes + parity checks; Week 3-4: canary UI and dashboard updates; Week 5+: backfill historical partitions and cleanup. Adjust if DB profiling shows issues.

maya: fine by product. Please get RFC + schema PR up today so we can review. Also include migration runbook for infra on-call in case index build causes load spikes.

jordan: PR incoming in ~2 hours. I'll attach a checklist and the parity tests. Thanks all.

liam: ack, will start staging tests.

rebecca: I'll draft the canary communication and the product acceptance criteria.

infra-bot: Reminder: open a DB maintenance ticket before starting long-running concurrent index builds.

jordan: adding ticket link once created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123

maya: great, thx.
